speaker: Sarah
text: For this project we need to decide on our backend framework. I think FastAPI is the right choice because it gives us automatic API docs, async support, and great performance.

speaker: Raj
text: Agreed on FastAPI. It also plays nicely with Pydantic which we'll need for data validation.

speaker: Sarah
text: We'll use FastAPI for the backend. That's decided.

speaker: Sarah
text: Now we need someone to own the authentication layer. It needs to cover login, JWT token management, and user sessions.

speaker: Raj
text: I'll take care of the authentication layer.

speaker: Sarah
text: Great. Raj owns authentication. Let's keep the first version simple — no OAuth for now, just JWT-based auth.

speaker: Sarah
text: Let's keep the first version simple. We can iterate once the core is working.

speaker: Raj
text: Sounds good. I'll start on auth this week and have a draft ready for review by Wednesday.

speaker: Sarah
text: We need to pick a database for the new service. I've looked at MySQL and PostgreSQL and I think PostgreSQL is safer for us because of its better support for JSON fields, transactions, and its stricter data integrity constraints.

speaker: Raj
text: I agree, let's go with PostgreSQL. We've used it before and the team is already comfortable with it.

speaker: Sarah
text: PostgreSQL it is. It's also easier to host on Render and has good managed options on AWS if we need to scale.

speaker: Raj
text: I can set up the initial schema migrations with Alembic once authentication is done.

speaker: Sarah
text: We should also decide on our ORM. SQLAlchemy is the standard choice and it integrates well with FastAPI.

speaker: Raj
text: Agreed, SQLAlchemy with async support is the right call here.

speaker: Sarah
text: We need to get the API deployed before our demo. The deadline is Friday.

speaker: Sarah
text: We need the API deployed by Friday. No exceptions.

speaker: Raj
text: I'll handle the Render deployment. I've deployed on Render before and I know the environment variables and service config setup.

speaker: Sarah
text: Good. Raj is owning deployment to Render. Make sure the environment variables are all set correctly before go-live.

speaker: Raj
text: I'll also write the deployment runbook so anyone can reproduce it if needed.

speaker: Sarah
text: One thing to watch out for — make sure the PostgreSQL connection string is using the external URL on Render, not the internal one.

speaker: Raj
text: Got it. I'll double-check the database connection config before deploying.
